Finally, model checkpoint conversion is handled by [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_of_weights_to_jax.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_of_weights_to_jax.py) for converting OpenFold PyTorch weights to AlphaFold JAX-compatible [`.npz`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/train_openfold.py#L584) format, and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_v1_to_v2_weights.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_v1_to_v2_weights.py) for updating OpenFold checkpoints from older V1 to newer V2 key formats, ensuring compatibility and interoperability.

### Environment Setup and Third-Party Dependencies
The OpenFold repository includes scripts to manage its Conda environment and integrate essential third-party bioinformatics tools. The script [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/activate_conda_env.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/activate_conda_env.sh), which sources [`scripts/vars.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/activate_conda_env.sh#L3) to define [`ENV_NAME`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/vars.sh#L3), handles the activation of the OpenFold Conda environment by executing [`conda activate $ENV_NAME`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/activate_conda_env.sh#L5). Conversely, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh) provides a straightforward way to exit the active Conda environment using [`conda deactivate`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/deactivate_conda_env.sh#L3).

For setting up the necessary external dependencies, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh) orchestrates the installation of various tools and configurations. This script manages resources such as [`stereo_chemical_props.txt`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/setup.py#L133), prepares test data, installs OpenFold itself via [`python setup.py install`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/Dockerfile#L10), and clones [`NVIDIA/cutlass`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh#L17) (specifically version [`v3.6.0`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh#L17)). It also configures several environment variables critical for performance, including [`CUTLASS_PATH`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_third_party_dependencies.sh#L18), [`KMP_AFFINITY`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/docs/source/FAQ.md#L30), [`LIBRARY_PATH`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/docs/source/Installation.md#L23), and [`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/Dockerfile#L28). Additionally, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh) automates the cloning, building, and installation of [`hh-suite`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh#L3) (branch [`v3.3.0`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh#L3)) from GitHub, placing it in [`/opt/hhsuite`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/install_hh_suite.sh#L6) and creating necessary symlinks in [`/usr/bin`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/train_openfold.py#L522) for system-wide access. This setup ensures that tools like HHblits and HHsearch, which are vital for generating features such as Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs), are correctly integrated. More details on how these external tools are used can be found in [Bioinformatics Tool Wrappers](#bioinformatics-tool-wrappers).

### Comprehensive Database Download and Preparation
The OpenFold codebase includes a suite of scripts designed to download, extract, and prepare various biological sequence and structure databases essential for protein structure prediction. These databases range from those originally used by AlphaFold to specialized resources for OpenFold's specific requirements. The primary entry point for managing these downloads is the [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts) directory, which contains shell scripts and Python utilities for orchestrating the entire data preparation pipeline.

A core script, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_alphafold_dbs.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_alphafold_dbs.sh), acts as an orchestrator for downloading most AlphaFold-related databases. It allows users to choose between a full or reduced set of databases and subsequently calls dedicated sub-scripts for each resource. For instance, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_bfd.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_bfd.sh) and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_small_bfd.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_small_bfd.sh) handle the acquisition of the BFD database (Big Fantastic Database) in its full or smaller version, respectively. Similarly, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_mgnify.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_mgnify.sh) fetches the MGnify database, and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_pdb70.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_pdb70.sh) is responsible for the PDB70 database.

For protein structure data, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_pdb_mmcif.sh) downloads and processes the entire PDB mmCIF archive, flattening its directory structure for easier access. The script also handles the acquisition of the [`obsolete.dat`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/train_openfold.py#L537) file, which tracks obsolete PDB entries. A related utility, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_pdb_seqres.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_pdb_seqres.sh), specifically downloads and filters the PDB SeqRes database to include only protein sequences.

Beyond AlphaFold's original data, OpenFold also leverages and provides scripts for its own model parameters and specialized resources. For instance, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_params.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_params.sh) and its alternatives, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_params_gdrive.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_params_gdrive.sh) and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_params_huggingface.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_params_huggingface.sh), are used to obtain pre-trained OpenFold model weights from various sources. The SoloSeq model parameters and corresponding ESM-1b embeddings are downloaded via [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_soloseq_params.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_openfold_soloseq_params.sh) and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_soloseq_embeddings.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_soloseq_embeddings.sh), respectively.

Databases crucial for sequence alignment, such as Uniref and Uniclust, are managed through scripts like [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniref30.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniref30.sh), [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniref90.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniref90.sh), and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniclust30.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniclust30.sh). For multimer predictions, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniprot.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_uniprot.sh) downloads and merges the UniProt TrEMBL and SwissProt databases into a single FASTA file.

The system also integrates specific resources like the ColabFold environmental database, downloaded by [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_colabfold_envdb.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_colabfold_envdb.sh), which is part of a larger MMseqs2-related download process initiated by [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_mmseqs_dbs.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_mmseqs_dbs.sh).

Beyond mere downloading, the scripts also include utilities for transforming data. For example, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/data_dir_to_fasta.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/data_dir_to_fasta.py) converts directories of protein structure files (CIF, PDB, or ProteinNet [`.core`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/unpack_proteinnet.py#L8)) into a single FASTA file, extracting amino acid sequences and handling chain identification. [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_cameo.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_cameo.py) specifically downloads CAMEO protein data, including CIF files and FASTA sequences, with options for filtering by sequence length. The [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_roda_pdbs.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/download_roda_pdbs.sh) script downloads CIF files relevant to RODA alignments and reports any missing files. These scripts collectively ensure that the OpenFold environment has access to the necessary data in appropriate formats for both training and inference pipelines.

### Advanced Alignment Generation and Processing
Protein sequence alignment generation in OpenFold involves orchestrating multiple bioinformatics tools to produce the necessary input features for protein structure prediction. This process transforms raw protein sequence data into rich alignments that capture evolutionary and structural information. The scripts handle various aspects, from parsing different input formats to precomputing alignments and processing intermediate files, with support for both local and distributed execution environments.

The system utilizes specialized scripts to manage the complex workflow of generating alignments. For instance, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/precompute_alignments.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/precompute_alignments.py) is central to orchestrating the precomputation of protein sequence alignments. This script integrates a range of tools, including JackHMMER, HHblits, HMMsearch, and HHSearch, to generate comprehensive Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs). It can parse diverse input formats such as mmCIF, FASTA, and ProteinNet [`.core`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/unpack_proteinnet.py#L8) files, and is designed to leverage multithreading and distributed execution (via SLURM variables) to handle large datasets efficiently.

A specialized script, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh), focuses on utilizing [`MMSEQS`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L4) for protein sequence searching and MSA generation. This script executes a multi-step [`MMSEQS`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L4) workflow, which includes commands like [`search`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/train_openfold.py#L481), [`expandaln`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L45), [`align`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/kalign.py#L50), [`filterresult`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L49), and [`result2msa`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L50). It generates [`.a3m`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L56) files for Uniref and environmental databases, as well as [`.m8`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/colabfold_search.sh#L57) files for PDB templates, crucial for identifying homologous structures. The script manages temporary directories and files, ensuring a clean working environment, and allows for flexible parameterization of search and alignment thresholds.

Another script, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/precompute_alignments_mmseqs.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/precompute_alignments_mmseqs.py), specifically precomputes alignments using [`MMseqs2`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/docs/source/index.md#L51) in conjunction with [`HHsearch`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/docs/source/original_readme.md#L390). It processes input FASTA sequences, splits [`.a3m`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/data_modules.py#L56) files, and generates [`pdb70_hits.hhr`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/docs/source/Aux_seq_files.md#L29) files, which are essential for downstream template-based modeling.

For managing the resulting alignment data, OpenFold includes [Protein Alignment Database Management](#openfold-management-scripts-protein-alignment-database-management) scripts. These scripts create, extend, and consolidate protein alignment databases. For instance, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py) consolidates alignment files into a single binary database and a JSON index, while [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py) generates sharded alignment databases, particularly useful for managing extremely large datasets. The sharding process utilizes parallel execution for shard creation and file reading. Furthermore, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py) combines multiple individual index files into a single "super index," and [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py) extends this super index to include non-unique protein chains by mapping identical sequences to existing alignment entries.

The system also includes a specific script, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/slurm_scripts`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/slurm_scripts), for generating Uniclust30 all-against-all alignments on SLURM clusters. This script efficiently handles large-scale alignment tasks by transferring databases to local SSDs, filtering already-processed entries, splitting inputs across nodes, executing [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) in parallel, and compressing the results. This distributed approach optimizes performance for computationally intensive alignment jobs.

### Protein Alignment Database Management
OpenFold includes a set of specialized scripts for the creation, management, and consolidation of protein alignment databases. These databases are designed to optimize data retrieval for model training and inference by storing precomputed sequence alignments in an efficient, indexed format. The system addresses challenges such as handling large datasets through sharding and intelligently managing non-unique protein chains.

A core component is the consolidation of precomputed alignment files into a single binary database file ([`.db`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py#L7)) with a corresponding JSON index file ([`.index`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/np/residue_constants.py#L1148)). This process is handled by scripts such as [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db.py). This script iterates through directories containing individual protein chain alignments, reads the raw file bytes, and records metadata such as filenames, byte offsets, and lengths into the index. The index maps each protein chain's alignment directory to a list of tuples containing this file information.

For very large datasets, the system supports sharded alignment databases. The script [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/create_alignment_db_sharded.py) generates such a sharded database, leveraging parallel processing to create individual shards. This script also generates a "super index" (a JSON dictionary) that maps each chain name to its corresponding database file and provides file information necessary for retrieval. This sharding mechanism helps manage memory and I/O efficiently.

To combine multiple smaller alignment database indices into a cohesive whole, the script [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py) is utilized. It aggregates individual [`.index`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/np/residue_constants.py#L1148) files into a single [`super.index`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/docs/source/original_readme.md#L476) file, which maps sequence identifiers to their respective database names and file data, simplifying access across multiple database sources.

Optimizing data retrieval further, OpenFold includes a mechanism for handling non-unique protein chains. The script [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/add_non_unique_to_alignment_db.py) extends an existing [`super_index`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py#L10) to include these chains. It identifies chains without direct alignments but with sequences identical to chains that do have alignments. For these non-unique chains, the [`super_index`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/alignment_db_scripts/unify_alignment_db_indices.py#L10) is updated to point to the existing alignment entries of their identical counterparts, effectively reducing redundancy and storage requirements while ensuring all chains can access relevant alignment data.

These scripts collectively streamline the process of preparing and accessing large-scale protein alignment data, which is fundamental for both training and inference tasks within the OpenFold framework. For details on how alignments are initially generated, refer to [Advanced Alignment Generation and Processing](#openfold-management-scripts-advanced-alignment-generation-and-processing).

### DeepSpeed Configuration and Inference Utilities
OpenFold leverages DeepSpeed to manage and optimize model configuration and inference, particularly for large models that require efficient resource utilization. Scripts within the repository dynamically generate DeepSpeed configuration files and facilitate testing DeepSpeed's inference capabilities.

Configuration of DeepSpeed is handled by the script [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py). This script constructs a JSON configuration based on command-line arguments, allowing users to specify various optimization settings. These settings include details for optimizers (e.g., [`Adam`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/train_openfold.py#L220), [`OneBitAdam`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L28)), learning rate schedulers ([`LRRangeTest`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L49), [`OneCycle`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L49), [`WarmupLR`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L49), [`WarmupDecayLR`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L50)), and different mixed-precision training modes ([`fp16`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L271), [`bfloat16`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L275), [`amp`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/build_deepspeed_config.py#L266)). It also enables advanced memory and computation optimizations such as activation checkpointing (partitioning activations and CPU offloading) and ZeRO optimization (Zero Redundancy Optimizer) for memory efficiency. Furthermore, the script supports configuring a FLOPs profiler to analyze model performance and gradient clipping to stabilize training. This dynamic generation of configuration files simplifies the process of adapting DeepSpeed to diverse training and inference scenarios.

For testing DeepSpeed's inference capabilities, the script [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/deepspeed_inference_test.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/deepspeed_inference_test.py) provides a mechanism to validate the setup. It initializes a dummy neural network model and dataset, then configures DeepSpeed for inference using [`deepspeed.init_inference`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/deepspeed_inference_test.py#L44). This allows developers to confirm that DeepSpeed is correctly integrated and can efficiently perform forward passes, potentially leveraging model parallelism across multiple GPUs. This testing mechanism ensures that the chosen DeepSpeed configurations are functional before deployment with the full OpenFold model.

### Model Checkpoint Conversion
OpenFold includes scripts for converting model checkpoints between various formats, which facilitates compatibility with different frameworks and model versions. This functionality is essential for users who wish to leverage pre-trained OpenFold models within DeepMind's AlphaFold JAX environment or adapt models trained with older OpenFold versions.

One conversion script, located at [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_of_weights_to_jax.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_of_weights_to_jax.py), handles the transformation of OpenFold's PyTorch-based checkpoint files (typically [`.pt`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/thread_sequence.py#L141) files) into the NumPy-based [`.npz`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/train_openfold.py#L584) format used by the AlphaFold JAX framework. This process involves reshaping and reordering parameters to match AlphaFold's expected weight layout, as OpenFold and AlphaFold may use different internal representations for model weights. The script utilizes a parameter translation mechanism to map OpenFold parameter names to their AlphaFold equivalents and then applies specific reshaping functions based on the parameter type (e.g., linear layer weights, multi-head attention weights). By doing so, it ensures that an OpenFold-trained model can be seamlessly loaded and used for inference within the AlphaFold JAX codebase.

Another script, [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_v1_to_v2_weights.py`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/convert_v1_to_v2_weights.py), addresses compatibility issues between different versions of OpenFold checkpoints. Specifically, it converts checkpoints from a deprecated V1 key format to a V2 format. This is relevant for users who might have models trained with older OpenFold implementations and need to update them for use with newer OpenFold versions that expect the V2 key structure. The script supports both PyTorch Lightning and DeepSpeed checkpoint formats. For DeepSpeed checkpoints, it also manages the conversion of optimizer states and parameter shapes, which are crucial for resuming training or inference with the updated model. These conversion utilities help maintain backward compatibility and interoperability across different stages of model development and deployment.

### SLURM-based Uniclust30 Alignment Generation
The generation of Uniclust30 all-against-all alignments on SLURM clusters is managed by the [`/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/slurm_scripts/run_uniclust30_search.sh`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/scripts/slurm_scripts/run_uniclust30_search.sh) script. This script is designed to efficiently distribute and execute the demanding [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) search operations across multiple nodes in a high-performance computing environment.

The process begins by transferring the Uniclust30 database files to a local SSD on each compute node. This step is performed to minimize I/O bottlenecks and accelerate [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) execution. To prevent redundant computations, the script identifies and filters out protein entries that have already been processed, ensuring that [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) only runs on new or incomplete alignment tasks.

The filtered input data is then split into node-specific chunks, allowing each SLURM node to process a distinct subset of the Uniclust30 database. This division of labor enables parallel execution of [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30). A semaphore mechanism is employed to control the number of concurrent [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) instances on each node, optimizing resource utilization.

As [`hhblits`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/openfold/data/tools/hhblits.py#L30) generates alignments, the script periodically checks the size of the temporary scratch directory. To manage storage effectively, results are compressed into [`.zip`](https://github.com/aqlaboratory/openfold/notebooks/OpenFold.ipynb#L807) archives in a designated output directory, and the temporary scratch directories are cleaned up. This systematic approach ensures efficient data management and scalability for large-scale alignment generation. For broader context on managing OpenFold's operational scripts, see [OpenFold Management Scripts](#openfold-management-scripts).
